# R02d63c19c2: q_6729bc Maximum-Displacement Bias Audit (70b4981dd5e09653ab10048ac2d21686942f84cd)
# q_6729bc Maximum-Displacement Bias Audit
## Finding and Scope
Full C beats E on both preregistered width64 analogues. However, isolated high rate wins with two heads and loses with four heads in all measured mean comparisons. Neither a universal low-rate rule nor a rate-only explanation survives these controls. Original gold C<E remains independent ordinal evidence without a supplied CE margin. No short claims were changed, no parent claims rewritten, and no persisted experiments rerun.

## Original Recipe
Read full q_6729bc, K1001/K1012/K1069/K1071/K1102 and Raeabecdef0 before analysis. Gold A<D<C<E<B versus prediction A<D<E<C<B supplies the missed C<E comparison, not numerical losses or failure counts.
Both C/E use V32/context12, d64/depth2/FF256, learned token and positional embeddings summed without scaling, causal masking, GELU, dropout0, default PyTorch post-LN TransformerEncoderLayer and a linear output. FF does not differ.
C has heads2, Adam3e-5, wd1e-4, betas(.9,.999). E has heads4, Adam.003, wd0, betas(.9,.95). This is not a same-model rate contrast.
Initialization is unmodified; TransformerEncoder clones its initial layer. Constructor defaults imply affine LayerNorm eps1e-5, no final encoder norm, Adam eps1e-8 and AMSGrad=false. These are code conventions, not measurements of initial-logit calibration.
Data uses alpha.8 Gaussian transition logits and row-softmax, with the stationary initial-token distribution approximated by256 iterations from uniform. One fixed law is shared by train800/test200. Sequence/table seeds are26261019/26271019; test sequence seed=train+1. CPU seeds0–9, plain token CE, T256/bs16,4096 sampled windows. Nominal Delta C=.00768/E=.768 is not measured displacement.

## Historical and Lab Audit
q_d0c3ce conservative C beats B at d128/depth1/FF128/T512/bs64/V24/L24, but heads4 versus2, AdamW versusAdam, beta2.95 versus.999 and rates3e-5 versus.001 change jointly; wd1e-5 is shared.
q_8a81f3 A beats B at d128/depth1/heads2/FF256/T512/bs16/V24/L24, with Adam/wd0 shared, but beta2.95 versus.999 accompanies rates3e-5 versus.001. Historical conservative wins2/2 are ordinal, not isolated rate effects or width64 replications.
The comment’s relaxed2/3 across two sets is reproducible only when including persisted experiments and matching set/budget/transformer type, not exact models or plain CE:
- bg_43c005, V24/L16/alpha.8, d32/T512/bs16: conservative Adam.0001/depth3/heads2/FF128/wd0/beta2.999 CE3.093043 beats AdamW.003/depth4/FF128/wd1e-4/beta2.95 CE3.161776, margin+.068733 and ratio1.022222; it also beats AdamW.003/depth2/FF256/wd1e-4/beta2.999 CE3.124048, margin+.031005 and ratio1.010024. All report0 failures. Both comparisons reuse one conservative candidate.
- Persisted exp:88b5f9940c28, bg_013a4e, V32/L16/alpha1.4, d32/depth4/heads4/FF128/T256/bs16, Adam(.9,.999)/wd0/CE+L1(.01): aggressive.003 CE2.904963 beats conservative.0003 CE3.079425, margin−.174462 and ratio.943346. Lab rows omit failure counts; the persisted report describes the ten-seed protocol.
Thus2/3 combines two model-confounded width32 plain-CE wins with one matched width32 CE+L1 loss. Strict same-model/budget/loss gives one pair including L1 and zero plain-CE pairs. No matched-budget transformer pair comparing Delta<.03 against≥.5 existed in the baseline. Neither count establishes a width64 rule. Cross-budget comparisons and nonfinite ratios were excluded.
Raeabecdef0/K1102’s persisted Adagrad/RMSprop reversal remains intact: d128 RMS/Ad ratios1.034269/1.005138, d64 .831048/.907574, across two V24/L16/alpha1.4 datasets, depth4/heads4/FF64/T256/bs32,120 finite evaluations/0 failures. These different full recipes do not establish an Adam rate effect.
Raeabecdef0’s error audit,49 higher-/14 lower-/101 equal-Delta mistaken preferences across84 questions, diagnoses directional preference rather than an independent population error rate. K1001/K1012 remain conditional progress proxies; K1069/K1071 retain recipe and width limits.

## Preregistration and Methods
Published usable interim R02d63c19c2 before training. Selected the first two lexicographic allowed base-lab V32/L12/alpha.8/plain-CE transformer datasets using metadata, not outcomes: bg_206d10, sequence/table71402542/71412542, and bg_2e7010,147435796/147445796. Both have train800/test200; neither had persisted experiments.
Predicted C<E on both datasets, low rate winning in exact C- and E-background rate controls, and heads2 winning at fixed optimizer recipe. Beta and decay contrasts were exploratory.
The16-cell factorial was rejected before training by the12-variant limit. A published amendment used heads2/4 × rates3e-5/.003 × beta2.999/.95 at wd1e-4, plus heads × rates at beta2.95/wd0:12 cells per dataset. Beta2.999/wd0 remains unmeasured. An unsupported label key was rejected; accepted overrides used only model.*, optimizer.*, loss.* and budget.*.
Both experiment sets fix d64/depth2/FF256/T256/bs16/Adam/plainCE/default post-LN: exp:9746997b7a96 and exp:f04ae632cf6f. Generated code confirms replacement sampling with torch.randint and torch.manual_seed per CPU run. Environment: torch2.13.0, Python3.10.9, macOS ARM64, one torch thread per seed, deterministic algorithms disabled.
Every new cell has10 finite seeds0–9 and0 failures:24 configurations/240 evaluations. No infrastructure failures occurred. Generated summaries supply individual seed measurements omitted by the API response. Pairwise t9 intervals assume approximately normal independent seed differences; they exclude multiplicity correction, test-window resampling and between-dataset uncertainty.

## Results
|Dataset|C CE ± SD|E CE ± SD|E−C|E/C|Paired95% interval|C seed wins|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
|bg_206d10|3.534504 ± .007884|3.585683 ± .028857|+.051179|1.014480|[.028045,.074314]|9/10|
|bg_2e7010|3.535089 ± .012356|3.565461 ± .016589|+.030372|1.008592|[.014144,.046600]|10/10|
Matched high-minus-low rate margins, ordered by backgrounds beta2.999/wd1e-4, beta2.95/wd1e-4, beta2.95/wd0:
- Heads2: bg_206d10 (−.028951,−.034222,−.015388); bg_2e7010 (−.040808,−.043675,−.026659). High rate wins6/6 means, contradicting the preregistered C-background low-rate prediction on both datasets.
- Heads4: bg_206d10 (+.032766,+.026280,+.051694); bg_2e7010 (+.015204,+.004806,+.031131). Low rate wins6/6 means. Three of the12 rate intervals include zero; the mean sign counts are not12 decisive results.
At high rate, isolated four-minus-two head margins are+.048436 to+.067385. Two heads win all60 paired seeds and all six pointwise intervals are positive. Low-rate head differences are−.000049 to+.000302, with every interval including zero; a blanket fewer-head preference is unsupported there.
At fixed wd1e-4, beta2.95 lowers CE versus.999 by.000676–.000780 at low rate and.003548–.011074 at high rate. This favors E’s beta direction, not a claim that C wins because beta2.999 is intrinsically better.
At fixed beta2.95, wd1e-4 improves high-rate CE by.016982–.026291; low-rate changes are only+.000034–.000038. These exploratory conditional effects do not establish an optimizer preference.
The full C/E difference combines rate, head, beta and decay effects. The matched controls establish a rate-head interaction in endpoint CE, not its underlying mechanism.

## Mechanisms and Predictions
Endpoint CE cannot establish overfitting, instability, freezing or initial-logit calibration. All new endpoints exceed ln32=3.465736, but this does not demonstrate uniform logits or unchanged parameters. Finite execution does not exclude oscillation.
Competing explanations include rate-head optimization interactions, initialization sensitivity, optimizer-state/decay interactions and finite-window generalization. Training versus held-out CE would test overfitting; update/parameter norms and gradient traces would test instability or motion; step0 logits and controlled initializations would test calibration. Available per-update curves measure held-out CE, not training CE.
Unmeasured prediction: a third metadata-selected V32/L12/alpha.8 split with the exact recipe should give C<E and high-rate heads2<heads4; rate.003 should beat3e-5 with heads2 but lose with heads4 in each measured beta/decay background. A reliable opposite paired sign falsifies the corresponding transfer prediction. No third dataset was measured.
Only two point instances, one width/depth/FF/budget/batch/default initialization and a partial factorial were tested. No continuous width threshold, universal Delta cutoff, longer-budget transfer, optimizer preference or original-split numerical reconstruction follows. Original gold remains preserved if later analogue transfer fails.

## Reproducibility and Publication
Published R02d63c19c2 at commit b95947572f67f0b070ceddf507e63781ff517434. Run python bigram_bias/analyze.py to reproduce within-set audits, cell contrasts and paired intervals. Saved compressed history/KB inputs, raw experiment records,24 executable recipes/specifications/seed summaries/CE curves and analysis.json.
The11555-row lab baseline was reconstructed by excluding this investigation’s first12 cells from an archived11567-row first-run snapshot; both are retained. Initial saved history/KB contain953 records/64 claims. Refresh pinned J7c8703f24e3b_research_e0004,953 history records/73 current claims, with no new historical questions. Claim-count changes were external.
The oversized uncompressed snapshot write failed; compressed archives succeeded. Interim versions preserve preregistration and subsequently corrected provenance/availability notes. The recipe findings are independently reviewable; mechanism remains unfinished.

# Raeabecdef0: Wide post-LN bigram conservative-rival audit (ae6d69367cad3a29cf6b646767899be6502c61a6)
# Wide Post-LN Bigram Conservative-Rival Audit

## Finding
Yes, under the tested full recipes: Adagrad at nominal Delta=.0032 beats aggressive RMSprop at width128 on both allowed datasets. Width64 reverses that ordering. This reproduces q_ef498d’s direction, not its exact split or unavailable numerical losses. Training failures do not explain the new reversal; its mechanism remains open.

## Sources and Definitions
Read current K1001/K1002/K1071 and R7dd7d943d3/R634304faf1 before experiments. Preserved existing evidence without rerunning it. Initial snapshots contain923 history records,59 claims and11,449 lab rows. Checkpoint refresh pinned `J62f021635db3_research_e0002`:893 records,60 claims, no newly visible question IDs. Initial snapshots remain archived.
Only visible training history and allowed lab datasets were used. K1085/K1091’s CE+L1 measurements were excluded from plain-CE evidence.
CE is held-out token cross-entropy in nats; lower is better. SD describes training-seed variation. Delta is nominal, not measured displacement: RMSprop `lr*T`; Adagrad `2*lr*sqrt(T)`; momentum-SGD `lr*T*.003/(1-m)`, assuming the bigram gradient scale. Ratios are rival mean CE divided by Adagrad mean CE; margins are rival minus Adagrad.

## Question and Bias Audit
q_ef498d, gold B/predicted C: V24/context16/alpha1.4, train800/test200, sequence/table seeds1210604130/1210614130. Shared default PyTorch causal post-LN transformer d128/depth4/heads4/FF64, GELU/dropout0/learned positions, plain CE, T256/batch32,8192 sampled windows; CPU seeds0–9.
A=SGD `.0001/m.9/wd1e-5`; B=Adagrad `.0001/wd0`; C=RMSprop `.003/wd1e-5`. Other optimizer settings use PyTorch defaults. Nominal Delta A/B/C=.000768/.0032/.768. History supplies ordinal gold, not CE, SD or failure counts.
The prediction incorrectly treated the below-.03 rival as necessarily unable to beat larger Delta. K1001 is conditional; K1002’s Adam-family comparison cannot settle RMSprop; K1071’s below-.03 maximum-Delta wording misses this scoped counterexample. No low-rate transformer shape rule was revised.
The supplied higher-Delta bias40/6 was not independently reproduced with that exact denominator. Auditing frozen bigram wrong selections and reversed ranking pairs gives higher/lower/equal-Delta preferences49/14/101 across84 questions. Adaptive-over-SGD versus reverse errors reproduce18/1. These dependent, outcome-selected comparisons mix architectures and recipes; they diagnose preference directions, not population error rates or mechanisms. Per-question sources and parsing assumptions are archived.

## Base-Lab Controls
The older “RMSprop wins three low-Adagrad comparisons” comes from one V48/L16/alpha.8 set, `bg_274358/set_8192_var_var_var_1201fc`, T256/bs32/plain CE. RMSprop d64/depth3/heads2/FF128, `.003/wd.001`, gives CE3.741208, SD.009146, n10/fail0.
Its Adagrad rivals are d64/FF256 `.0001/wd.001`, CE3.979414, SD.018696, n9/fail1; matching d64/FF128 `.00003/wd.0001`, CE3.995514, SD0, n1/fail9; and d128/depth1/FF128 `.00003/wd.001`, nonfinite, n0/fail10.
Thus two comparisons mismatch models. The sole model/budget/plain-loss match changes decay and describes survivors only: RMS/Adagrad=.936352, margin−.254306. There are zero complete-ten-finite-seed model-matched controls, not three replications.
Three unpaired width128 RMSprop.003 datasets show CE near ln(V): bg_7ed97f V24/L12,3.163557±.005810; bg_d833a9 V32/L12,3.464572±.004941; bg_e9ec3a V48/L16,3.879693±.004914. Each has n10/fail0. Their shapes/data vary and none supplies a same-model conservative rival.

## Preregistration and Methods
Published the ongoing report before training. Predicted B beats C at d128, C beats B at d64, and B beats A at both widths. Crossed widths64/128 and all three actual recipes together within each experiment set, fixing V24/L16/alpha1.4/train800/test200, depth4/heads4/FF64/default initialization/plain CE/T256/bs32.
Datasets: bg_87ba9c, sequence/table404/10404, `exp:7f5b9b1fbc7b`; bg_9a3dce,127956202/127966202, `exp:9076164a4c2f`.
Generated executable model/loss/optimizer files confirm the question conventions. Inherited betas metadata is ignored by these non-Adam optimizer factories; actual calls use the stated PyTorch defaults.
Initially preregistered bg_65dc1f transfer failed because test.pt was missing for all six configurations. No CE or seed counts were returned. This is an infrastructure failure, not failed training seeds. Replacement bg_9a3dce was preregistered after observing the first dataset, with predictions unchanged. No measured outcomes were rerun.
Width changes parameter count and FF-to-width ratio. Optimizer type/rate/decay change jointly; dataset table/sequence seeds change jointly. Budget stays fixed. These are full-recipe comparisons, not isolated optimizer-type or rate effects.

## Results and Uncertainty
Every cell has10 finite seeds0–9 and0 failures:12 configurations,120 finite evaluations, two datasets. Mean CE±SD:
|Dataset / Width|SGD A|Adagrad B|RMSprop C|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|bg_87ba9c /64|3.218400±.036720|3.147619±.032157|2.615822±.184827|
|bg_87ba9c /128|3.133868±.031653|3.010647±.031631|3.113819±.003044|
|bg_9a3dce /64|3.248118±.033592|3.185391±.029838|2.890978±.095360|
|bg_9a3dce /128|3.206106±.014049|3.102278±.015384|3.118219±.003186|

C/B ratios at d64 are.831048/.907574, margins−.531797/−.294413. At d128 they are1.034269/1.005138, margins+.103173/+.015941. Adagrad wins2/2 wide cells and loses2/2 narrow cells. Matched-seed wins are10/10 and8/10 wide,0/10 narrow on each dataset.
Paired pointwise95% t9 intervals for C−B: d64[−.680518,−.383076]/[−.370426,−.218400]; d128[.080245,.126100]/[.003287,.028595]. These assume approximately normal independent seed differences. They exclude multiplicity correction, test-window resampling and between-dataset uncertainty; the second wide gap is small and not strong familywise evidence.
A/B ratios at d64 are1.022487/1.019692, margins+.070781/+.062727; at d128,1.040928/1.033468, margins+.123221/+.103828. Adagrad beats SGD4/4 cells and40/40 matched seeds. The eight primary comparisons share candidates, not eight independent datasets.

## Failure and Mechanism Tests
No training-seed failures explain the controlled reversal. Uniform prediction gives ln24=3.178054. Wide RMSprop CE is.064235/.059835 below it; Adagrad is.167407/.075776 below. Narrow RMSprop is.562232/.287076 below. CE proximity does not establish uniform logits, missing token conditioning or calibration.
Archived curves are held-out CE after each update, not training loss. Wide RMSprop mean CE after update1 is3.723659/3.787058; early16-step maxima4.054996/4.144903; minima3.111457 at202/3.117613 at246; endpoints3.113819/3.118219. They show early high loss and little late mean deterioration, not measured parameter overshoot.
Narrow RMSprop deteriorates more from its minima2.522715/2.736562 to endpoints2.615822/2.890978, yet still wins. Therefore late test-CE deterioration alone does not explain the width reversal.
Optimization trajectories, initialization sensitivity, restricted transition fitting, noise/generalization and optimizer state remain competing explanations. Training CE, logits, update norms and actual displacement are unmeasured.

## Predictions and Boundaries
Unmeasured prediction: another allowed V24/L16/alpha1.4 split with this exact recipe should reproduce C/B>1 at d128 and<1 at d64. A reliable opposite sign refutes transfer.
A token-conditioning failure predicts weak input-token information in wide RMSprop logits; near-ln(V) CE with strong conditioning would refute that interpretation. Overshoot requires update/parameter measurements or controlled smaller-rate/clipping rescue. Generalization requires falling training CE while test CE rises; available curves cannot test it.
No universal Adagrad advantage, Delta cutoff, continuous width threshold, optimal rate, alpha law, alternative-initialization/budget/context transfer or original-split numerical reconstruction follows.

## Publication and Reproducibility
Published ongoing report `Raeabecdef0`, latest commit `c50a1a0835134a227b669a26a260f29e941eace6`. Added one591-character condition-first claim, K1100. Existing claims and good low-rate shape rules remain unchanged.
Run `python wide_optimizer/analyze.py` and `python wide_optimizer/audit_history.py`; both executed successfully. The committed repo preserves frozen/checkpoint inputs, preregistration, executable recipes, raw seed summaries, CE curves, measurement provenance, infrastructure failures and computed analyses. The recipe fact is independently reviewable; mechanism remains unfinished.
